about: The balance gate's bands (tools/balance-check.mjs). Each band records what the game IS, with room for an 80-seed sample - measured on 120 seeds in docs/lab/damage-model-2026-09-18.md. A band is moved in the PR that means to move the game, and its `why` says so. ALL OF THEM MOVED on 2026-09-18 (D37): the chassis costs three times what it did and its upgrades six tenths, every body is plated from wave 6, energy goes through armour, resistances are wide, and Standard and Grim were re-fitted behind that. AMENDED the same evening (D38, docs/lab/energy-door-2026-09-18.md): plating has a twin for energy hits and three bodies are insulated; the E bands are new, both thermometers moved, and S3 reads 89% of 120 where it read 93%.

bands.why: A player who knows nothing - one plain Bolt by the entry, then nothing - holds Calm's wave 5. The stranger test plays Calm to wave 5 unaided. Unmoved by D37 on purpose: plating begins at wave 6. Measured 99% of 120.
...and then loses, having seen the game. Measured 1% of 120.
The base world's mixed line, bought depth first and going on, wins Calm. Measured 100% of 120.

D37: plain Bolts at the choke, never upgraded, as many as Scrap allows, do NOT win Standard. They won it 99% until 2026-09-18. Measured 3% of 120. If this band goes red, width is winning again - look at chassis prices and plating before anything else.
The same on Grim: 84% until 2026-09-18, 0% of 120 after.
Three plain Bolts by the entry and nothing more do not win Standard. Measured 0% of 120.

FLOOR RAISED 86% -> 89% with Standard x1.12 -> x1.105 (docs/lab/standard-curve-2026-09-18.md): measured 93% of 120 and 91% of the gate's 80 again, and the floor now sits two seeds under that - so the line sliding back to the bottom of its range, which took two unrelated PRs one evening, is a red gate and not a note in a document. History:The mixed line wins Standard most of the time - fitted to the UPPER end of 85-95% on purpose, because the lab's player buys the instant it can afford and places by arithmetic, and a person does neither. Measured 93% of 120 at x1.12; 89% of 120 after D38 (its Frost's energy hit meets plating now) - inside the 85-95% the fit was held to, no longer at its top; 86% of 120 once the lab's base world dealt commons alone, as the app's does (docs/lab/synergy-2026-09-18.md) - the floor of that range, and the next PR's subject.

L5, met for the first time: Grim is LOST by the base world. Measured 11% of 120 at x1.17 (18% holding six commons). It was 91-97% until 2026-09-18, and no curve could move it while width was unbounded. 3% of 120 once the lab stopped dealing the base world rares and epics it cannot have (D29) - the 11% was a richer world than a player without the workshop is in.
...and WON by the tree: the same line with the whole workshop bought and six relics held at the epic band. Measured 99% of 120. A ceiling - the relics are held from wave 1.

D37: 'I'm happy with bolt only builds if a combo of relics supports it, to find broken synergies.' Plain Bolts, never upgraded, holding the six commons that carry them (Payload, Penetrators, Hot Loads, Quick Hands, Wide Net, Bounty Hunter) win Standard. It read 1% until #365. Measured 83% of 120 (docs/lab/synergy-2026-09-18.md) - and 83% again at x1.105 with Payload 11 -> 10, which is why Payload moved: the easier curve alone took the set to 93%. It takes the SET: Payload alone 13%, the pair 19%. The top of the band is there because a set that always wins is no longer a find.

The door #365 could open: the base world's mixed line holding the same six commons must still LOSE Grim (S4). Measured 20% of 120, against 17% holding the six commons that suited a Bolt before. Un-gated, Payload took this row to 71% in the bounding round - which is why it reaches only a tower whose own hit is under 10. If this band goes red, look at Penetrators first: pierce is the half of the pair that a Railbore also enjoys.

D38, the mirror of S1: Ice Shards at the choke and no further - a 4-damage ENERGY hit, the cheapest in the game - as many as Scrap allows, do NOT win Standard. They won it 21% of 80 while plating let energy through (plain Bolts: 4%). Measured 2% of 120 (docs/lab/energy-door-2026-09-18.md). If this band goes red, energy width is winning again - look at COMBAT_RULES.insulating before anything else.
The same on Grim: 3% of 80 before D38, 0% of 120 after.

MOVED by #365, 25% -> 34% of 120: the pool can now deal Payload, and an Ice Shard is a 4-damage hit - the lab takes option 0 of every offer, so some of these runs find it. A relic-carried width build is what D37 welcomed; it is recorded because it is the energy door again.The same width holding the tree's six epic relics. It won Grim 94% of 80 before D38 - where plain Bolts holding the same relics won none - and this is the number that showed the door was open. Measured 25% of 120 after. NOT a target met: it is a reading, recorded so that it cannot drift back up unseen. What is left is a slow field seventy towers deep and the rule that a hit is never below 1.

D38's third target: a mono-energy tree build (Frost, Tesla, Laser - not one kinetic hit), played depth first holding the same relics as S4-grim-tree, loses to the mixed line. Measured 84% of 120 against the mixed tree line's 98%; holding nothing it is 2% against 18%. The band's top sits under S4-grim-tree's floor on purpose.

MOVED 11.90 -> 12.88 over 80 by Standard x1.12 -> x1.105, and meant to - the thermometer doing its job: five thousandths of growth a wave is a wave of life. Before that, MOVED 12.96 -> 11.90 by the lab's rarity cap (the probe takes option 0 of every offer, and the base world no longer deals it rares and epics) and by two relics joining the pool - an instrument correction, not a change to the game a player meets.NOT a player: six towers laid chassis first, then upgraded, then nothing - played to wave 40. It dies mid-run, so its mean death wave moves with the smallest change to a curve, a price or a road, where the win rates above sit near 0% or 100% and do not. Measured 12.96 over 80 (13.68 before D38, 25.20 before D37); half a wave either side. MOVED by D38 and meant to: one of its six towers is a Frost with Shatterfield, and its energy hit now meets plating like any other.

Re-centred 10.64 -> 10.30 over 80 with the Standard one, for the same two reasons.The same thermometer on Grim. Measured 10.64 over 80 (10.82 before D38, 21.85 before D37) - inside its old band, re-centred anyway so that it stays half a wave either side of what the game is. Proven in PR #360: a nudge of x0.01 to Grim's growth moves it most of a wave.
